description:
PLAN.md §6 (lines 184-193) describes the onSuccessSetIsDefault behaviour:
- After a successful Calendar/set (all creates/updates/destroys succeeded), if onSuccessSetIsDefault is a valid Calendar id, the handler calls set_default_calendar on the backend
- ParticipantIdentity/set has the same pattern via onSuccessSetIsDefault
- The PLAN names backend methods set_default_calendar and set_default_participant_identity

Neither method exists on CalendarsBackend (src/backend.rs has no such methods). The /set handlers do not parse onSuccessSetIsDefault from args. grep -rn 'onSuccessSetIsDefault\|set_default' crate-jmap-calendars-server/src returns nothing.

Spec basis: draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §3.3 (ParticipantIdentity/set) and the implied Calendar/set semantics referenced by PLAN. Cross-check the spec before implementing — Calendar/set onSuccessSetIsDefault is not on a quick search of the draft text and may be a PLAN.md hallucination; ParticipantIdentity/set onSuccessSetIsDefault is in §3.3.

Action: (1) confirm against draft text whether Calendar/set actually has onSuccessSetIsDefault; (2) confirm ParticipantIdentity/set §3.3 wire form; (3) implement whichever the spec requires; (4) add tests using the spec example JSON as oracle.

Wire impact: a client that uses onSuccessSetIsDefault gets back a /set response that does not flip the default — likely caught by a follow-up /get showing the wrong default. Annoying but not silent corruption.

Test gap: no inline test exercises any onSuccessSetIsDefault path.
title: Calendar/set and ParticipantIdentity/set onSuccessSetIsDefault unimplemented (PLAN.md §6)
